automatic_switchblade: Legal to own — ban repealed 11 Oct 2017 (PA 96 of 2017)
concealed_carry: FELONY for dagger/dirk/stiletto/double-edged non-folding — up to 5 yrs / $2500 (MCL 750.227(1))
vehicle_possession: Same felony applies in any vehicle occupied — reachable or not
preemption: NO — MCL 123.1102 covers firearms only; preemption bill vetoed 2021
named_city_ordinances: Detroit and Lansing restrict blades over 3 inches in public places
local_myth: That the 2017 switchblade repeal legalised concealed carry of everything. It did not — MI restricts by blade shape/function, not opening mechanism. Also: the '3-inch rule' in MCL 750.226 only applies once unlawful intent is proven; there is no general 3-inch limit.

automatic_switchblade: Legal since 1 Sept 2013 (HB 1862 removed switchblades from the prohibited list)
balisong: Legal — no separate balisong restriction; only the 5.5in location rule applies
gravity_otf: Legal — no separate gravity/OTF restriction after HB 1935
blade_length_limit: NONE for ordinary carry. Blade over 5.5in = 'location-restricted knife' (Penal Code 46.01(6)) — a LOCATION limit, not a carry limit
open_carry: Lawful at any blade length, subject to the location list for knives over 5.5in
concealed_carry: Lawful at any blade length, subject to the same location list
preemption: YES — Local Government Code 229.001 ('Firearms; Air Guns; Knives; Explosives') bars cities from stricter knife rules; narrow exception for riots/disasters
named_city_ordinances: Preempted — city ordinances stricter than state law are unenforceable
schools_gov_buildings: Location-restricted knives (over 5.5in) banned at: schools/educational institutions, 51% alcohol premises, high school/college/pro sporting events, correctional facilities, hospitals and nursing homes, amusement parks, places of religious worship. Most violations Class C misdemeanor max $500; SCHOOLS = third-degree felony, 2-10 years and up to $10,000
minors: Under 18 may not be sold a location-restricted knife, and may not carry one away from home, own property or own vehicle unless under direct supervision of a parent or legal guardian. Knives 5.5in and under: no age restriction
local_myth: That daggers, dirks, stilettos, poniards, swords, spears and Bowie knives are still 'illegal knives' in Texas. HB 1935 deleted that whole category effective 1 Sept 2017. Also: 5.5in is not a carry limit, it only decides WHERE you can carry.

automatic_switchblade: Legal under state law — Florida has no switchblade ban. Miami-Dade County has its own switchblade ordinance
blade_length_limit: NONE in statute. The '4 inches' figure comes from case law on what counts as a 'common pocketknife', not from a carry limit
open_carry: Generally lawful — s.790.053 targets firearms and electric weapons, not knives
concealed_carry: Since 1 July 2023 (HB 543) an eligible adult 21+ may carry a concealed knife WITHOUT a licence, if they meet the criteria for a Concealed Weapon Licence and carry valid ID. Before that, anything beyond a 'common pocketknife' needed a CWL
preemption: NO — s.790.33 preempts firearms and ammunition only, not knives
named_city_ordinances: Miami-Dade County switchblade ordinance; other municipalities may have their own
schools_gov_buildings: TO RESEARCH — schools and government buildings
minors: TO RESEARCH — permitless concealed carry under HB 543 requires 21+; under-21 rules need checking
local_myth: That you still need a Concealed Weapon Licence to carry any knife bigger than a 'common pocketknife'. That stopped being true on 1 July 2023 when HB 543 extended permitless concealed carry to weapons, knives included, for eligible adults 21+. Most knife-law pages online have not been updated.
